messages:
Maria (runtime): Quick sync — profiler and CI show a tail latency regression when we mix long and short sequences under continuous batching. Short requests are getting starved waiting for long tokens to finish. Posting traces + perf numbers, and tagging folks. @Alex R. can you check kernel selection angle? @Sam K. look at KV cache evictions.

Alex R.: Confirmed on perf CI: p99 up ~35% on mixed workload (70% short, 30% long). The queue shows short requests waiting 6–12ms extra while batches accumulate. Two obvious levers: (1) max wait time (flush sooner), (2) token-budget-based early flush so short requests don't get held for a super-long seq.

Sam K.: Observed high KV cache churn for some tenants: long sequences expand KV state and we see eviction thrash which triggers recompute kernels mid-stream. That spikes latency and distorts batching behavior. Suggest pinning recent KV pages for tenants with small-context hot traffic.

Nina S.: From SRE side we need an explicit fairness policy. Options: weighted round-robin at scheduling time, age-based priority boost for older requests, or per-tenant token budgets to stop a noisy tenant with long seqs from occupying batch slots. Also consider backpressure signals to clients.

Maria (runtime): Attaching a short profiler excerpt from a repro run (trimmed):

```
microprofile: mixed-70-30-2026-03-01
batch_size_avg: 12
wait_hist_ms: [0.5,1.2,3.5,8.1,15.7]
kernel_time_ms: { fused_attn: 4.3, generic_attn: 9.8, memcpy: 1.1 }
kv_ops: { hits: 72%, evict_count: 18 }
p99_latency_ms: baseline 22 -> mixed 30
```

Alex R.: That kernel_time breakdown is informative — when short and long are co-batched, we end up using generic_attn more often because the batch's max-seq forces a slower code path. Two possible mitigations: (A) sub-batch by sequence length and dispatch each sub-batch to the best kernel, or (B) enforce a token budget cap per batch and flush the remainder. Sub-batching cuts kernel inefficiency but increases scheduling overhead.

Sam K.: For KV: we can implement a small per-tenant pin list of recent KV keys. Heuristic: if tenant short_request_ratio > 0.6 and QPS > X, pin up to N entries. Also add a soft memory threshold to trigger aggressive shedding of long-context KV for low-priority tenants. Will draft policy.

Nina S.: We should codify fairness metrics in the console: p50/p95 by seq-length buckets and by tenant. Add a "starvation" alarm if average wait for short bucket > threshold for > 30s.

Alex R.: Prototype plan: implement sub-batch kernel routing in the runtime. Rough sketch: on batch formation, partition requests into 3 seq bins (short, med, long) by token_count; if short bin fills first, flush it immediately with fused kernels. Fallback: if flush would create tiny batches (<2), fall back to token-budget flush to avoid throughput loss.

Sam K.: KV pin config sketch:

```
kv_pinning:
  short_ratio_threshold: 0.6
  min_qps: 5
  max_pinned_entries: 128
  eviction_shedding_threshold_mb: 512
```

Nina S.: Perf test additions: add a mixed-workload scenario (70/30 short/long) + tenant skew (one tenant 60% of long seqs). Baseline current behavior, then run with sub-batch routing + KV pinning. Track p99, p50 short-bucket, and per-tenant p99.

Maria (runtime): Proposed scheduler changes (quick):
- default max_wait_ms: 8 (was 20)
- token_budget_target: 256 tokens per batch for fairness
- tenant_weighted_priority with aging boost after 5ms

Alex R.: Implementation note: kernel selection should be cheap — avoid per-request expensive checks. Use aggregated metrics per-formed batch during formation. Also consider JITing fused kernels for the common mixed shapes.

Sam K.: One perf caveat: pinning uses memory; we need guardrails so we don't push OOM on Dedicated nodes. We'll add a hard upper bound and memory reclaim path.

perf-bot: Ran synthetic perf scenario "mixed-70-30-tenant-skew" on staging: baseline p99=31.2ms, sub-batch prototype p99=24.1ms, kv-pinning-only p99=27.8ms, combined p99=22.6ms. Short-bucket p50 improved from 9.6ms -> 4.2ms combined.

Nina S.: Those staging numbers look promising. We should watch for throughput regressions under commodity GPUs though. Also validate behavior under many small tenants.

Maria (runtime): Action items: (1) Alex: prototype sub-batch kernel routing + measurement (2) Sam: draft KV pinning + memory guard rails (3) Nina: add perf scenario + alerts for starvation metrics. We'll reconvene EOD. If anyone sees a regression in the meantime, drop traces here. :+1: 

Alex R.: ACK, starting today.

Sam K.: I'll have a policy draft by EOD.

Nina S.: Adding perf job now.

Maria (runtime): Thanks all — let's aim to avoid any global defaults that favour long sequences by default. Fairness first. :rocket:
